title: Unfunded Migration Mandates
pattern: Infrastructure or platform teams releasing backwards-incompatible API changes and pushing the migration work onto downstream customer teams under a strict deadline.
why_bad: It creates a highly inefficient "unfunded mandate." Every downstream team must waste engineering hours learning the context and manually rewriting code, leading to duplicated effort, release delays, and resentment across the organization [725, 746, 747].
detection: The introduction of a breaking change in an internal shared dependency that requires manual downstream code modification across multiple repositories.
counterexample: Valid in small organizations where the total number of dependencies is low enough to be managed organically.
fix: Establish the "Churn Rule": the team introducing the breaking change is responsible for authoring and running automated transformations (Large Scale Changes) to migrate all callers themselves [714, 747, 748].
source: Software Engineering at Google, Chapter 1, 15, and 22 [270, 713, 714, 725, 746, 747, 748]
